newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps steady to firmer, mogas gains.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps steady to firmer, mogas gains.

text.p: NWE oil swaps were steady to a touch firmer on Friday. Heavy fuel was up $1, gasoline by up to $2 and naphtha by $1. Brent CFDs were several cents easier close in but firmer further out.
Traders said activity was fairly quiet with screen Brent consolidating after Thursday's slip.

Brent CFDs dropped by several cents in the prompt contract with July 14-18 pegged at -18 cents against August Brent from -13 cents and July 21-25 fell one cent to -24/25 cents from -23/24 cents. July 28 to August 1 was a touch firmer at -26 cents from -28 cents while August 4-8 firmed to -27 cents from -29 cents.
July 28- August 1 traded against September at - 25 cents.
Heavy fuel was about $1 a tonne firmer with July little talked around $85.50 while August was valued at $86.50. Wet barges traded up to $87 because of tightness.
Gasoline swaps were firmer taking support from physical tightness in NWE resulting from material arbing to the U.S. and some refinery maintenance.
July was fairly steady at $184.50 but the gains were shown more clearly in August which was valued between $185.50 and $186, up $1 and September at $184.50 and $185.
Naphtha swaps were also a touch firmer by $1 or so taking support from the stronger gasoline. Dealers said naphtha swaps were looking flat around $180-181 for July, August and September.
Gas oil crack spreads were heard at $4.20 for 4Q, off five cents from a Thursday trade and 1Q98 was talked at $4.40.
